topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture's place in the course and sets out its learning objectives before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Mutation, clonal evolution and cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations lead to cancer within a biological context that determines whether altered cells can expand.

topics.label: Environmental exposures and their contribution to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk against competing explanations based on chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the general mechanisms into a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why mutational initiation may require a subsequent growth-promoting environment for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Carcinogen specificity and biological susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the dependence of carcinogenic effects on biological context and conclude by consolidating the preceding mechanistic account.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence of carcinogenicity can be obtained and why the available methods cannot fully establish human cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as judgments about risks and benefits.
